To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fibrinolyic system of lung epithelium is involved in the pathogenesis and repair of ALI.

uPA-uPAR and PAI-I are expressed by lung alveolar epithelial cells and that uPA-mediated signaling regulates the expression of these proteins as well as that the tumor suppressor p53 is a trans-acting mRNA-binding protein that controls the expression of these fibrinolytic proteins. uPA-mediated signaling also controls the expression of p53 and regulates the viability of lung alveolar type II cells.
the uPA, uPA receptor, and PAI-I system of the lung epithelial cell regulates proteolysis and signaling and thereby influences the viability of the cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of uPA expression and its role in lung epithelial cell signaling and cellular viability.
the role of the uPA-uPA receptor system and its regulation in the pathogenesis and repair of lung injury and fibrosis.
the regulation of lung injury, inflammation, and repair by the uPA system, with particular attention to the roles of uPA and uPAR as signaling molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
uPA and uPAR are key mediators of lung epithelial proteolysis, cell signaling, and cell viability.
the fibrinolyte system and the regulation lung epithelial cell viability are intimately linked.
uPA-uPAR-mediated signaling is a key regulator of lung epithelial proteolysis, cell signaling, and cell viability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that uPA is not only a fibrinolytic enzyme, but also a signaling molecule that can regulate lung epithelial cell function and viability.

uPA, uPA, and PAI1 have important roles in the lung epithelial cell response to injury, including the regulation of proteolysis and signaling as well as cell viability, and that these effects are mediated through the regulation of mRNA stability and posttranslational changes in p53.
the uPA, uPA, and PAI1 axis in lung epithelial cell is a major regulator of the lung repair process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uPA, uPA, and PAI system in lung epithelium is not only important for fibrinolysis but also for lung epithelial cell signaling and survival.
the fibrinolytics system is not only a key component of lung homeostasis but also a major regulator of lung epithelial proteolysis, cell signaling, and cellular fate.

uPA, uPA, and PAI1 play an important role in the lung epithelism and the regulation of the lung epithelial cell viability. uPA is a serine protease that is involved in the degradation of the fibrin clot. uPAR is an integral membrane protein that binds uPA. uPAR also binds to vitronectin, an extracellular matrix protein that is involved in cell adhesion and migration.
